title: Grill — Task card UI overhaul (round 2)
summary:
Round 1 is recorded (15 recommendations accepted, 6 overridden). **5 follow-ups**: two of your notes opened new choices, and two of your picks conflict with something you'd want to see first.

Already settled from round 1: full redesign; titles keep their full wrap; progress = distinct steps with `✓ Done`; Primary only + `⋯` (Diff in the menu); keyboard dragging **in**; first-prose preview; one chip system, `h-7` buttons, `p-3`, one repo · branch line; you eyeball the dev build before merge.

proven.text: **Keyboard drops reuse the pointer drop path.** A keyboard drag ends in the same `onDragEnd`, so the pipeline-parent refusal (toast) and the server-409 re-sync apply unchanged, with no new drop rules.

proven: There is no `AGENTS.md` in the repo; `CLAUDE.md` is the agent rules file, so a card rule goes there (and/or a topic doc it points to).

questions.title: How should the designs be explored before one is picked?
questions.why: Your header answer and your mockup answer pull in different directions; this decides what Planning delivers before code.
questions.context: Round 1, header layout, you wrote: *"We actually need to follow the best practices and try some designs to make sure the new one won't have the 'breaking' issue."* But on the mockup question you picked *"one mockup of the chosen layout"*, and there is no chosen layout yet. Worst-case content in your DB: 26-char pipeline name, 25-char profile name, stack chip, every count badge, 128-char title (now unclamped), `Answer (12)`.

options.label: Planning publishes 2–3 whole-card alternatives, each measured; you pick one
options.description: Each alternative is rendered at the real 262 px width with the worst-case content above, in every card state, in light and dark. Each is checked automatically: every child inside the card box, nothing overlapping. The mockup shows pass/fail per state. My meta-footer layout is one of them.
options.consequence: One sign-off round with you before coding; the winner's measurements become the e2e bounds spec.

options.label: 2–3 alternatives, judged by eye only
options.consequence: Faster mockup; overflow is only caught later by the e2e spec.

options.label: The agent builds and measures alternatives, and shows me only the winner
options.consequence: No pick round; you only see one design.

recommendation.reason: Matches your 'try some designs' and 'make sure it won't break': the comparison is visual, and the non-breaking claim is measured, not eyeballed.

questions.title: Pipeline cards: how is the full pipeline name shown?
questions.why: Round 1 picked 'name truncates', but your note says the full name must be visible, so the pill design changes.
questions.context: Your note: *"We need full name been seen. We can even have it as a sub card to the main card. Or a special 'hat' in the UI when the card is a pipeline."* Already decided: progress never truncates, and the active step gets its own line.

options.label: A pipeline "hat": a full-width band at the top of the card
options.description: Tinted by run status (running/blocked/done/failed). Holds `⧉` + the full pipeline name (wraps if needed) and the progress (`3/10` or `✓ Done`) on the right. The active step / pending gate line sits at the bottom of the hat. The card body below looks like any other card.
options.consequence: Pipeline cards are recognisable at a glance; row 1 keeps only the type icon, count badges and stack chip, so it can't overflow.
options.preview:
┌───────────────────────────────┐
│▓⧉ Zebra Pipeline (No Audio)  3/10▓│
│▓▶ Implementing                  ▓│
├───────────────────────────────┤
│ ▣ 🤖2                       1/2 │
│ Acme Sync - Keep the inbox      │
│ watched for the whole session   │
│ …                               │

options.label: A sub-card (inset panel) inside the card, below the title
options.description: Bordered inset with the full name, progress and the active step.
options.consequence: Reads as 'attached run'; adds nested borders inside a 233 px box.

options.label: The pill moves to its own row in the header and wraps
options.consequence: Smallest change; a wrapped pill is an unusual shape.
options.preview:
│ ▣ 🤖2                       1/2 │
│ ⧉ Zebra Pipeline (No Audio) 3/10│
│ Acme Sync - Keep the inbox…     │

options.label: Mock up the hat and the sub-card as alternatives, and I'll pick from the mockup
options.consequence: Decided in the design round instead of now.

recommendation.reason: A hat gives the full name a full-width line without competing with other chips, and marks pipeline cards apart at a glance. It's your idea, and the cleanest fit for 233 px.

questions.title: Where does the 'don't break the card' rule live?
questions.why: Your note asked for a CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md rule; CLAUDE.md keeps only rules every task needs and points to a topic doc for the rest.
questions.context: Your note on header layout: *"It'd be important to also have in the Claude or Agents MD a rule for checking the card design to make sure a change is not turning that broken."*

options.label: A short rule in CLAUDE.md's *Webview* rules + a new `docs/architecture/task-card.md` + a Topic map row
options.description: The doc holds the layout contract: the 262 px card / 233 px content budget, no `shrink-0` on a variable-length chip, the per-state button table, the hat, the e2e bounds spec and how to run it.
options.consequence: Every agent sees the rule; the details sit where CLAUDE.md says subsystem contracts go.
options.preview:
- **A TaskCard change must keep every child inside the card in every state.**
  Run `e2e/task-card-bounds.spec.ts` (worst-case names, every badge, every
  action state, light and dark) before merging; it fails on any overflow.
  Layout contract: [task-card.md](docs/architecture/task-card.md).

options.label: The rule in CLAUDE.md only, no topic doc
Topic doc + Topic map row only, no rule bullet

recommendation.reason: The rule has to fire for anyone touching the card; the contract is too long for CLAUDE.md, which already sends subsystem detail to docs/architecture/.

sections.title: Action row & keyboard (consequences of round-1 picks)

questions.title: With 'Primary only + ⋯', confirm the per-state buttons, in particular Stop on a pending human gate
questions.why: This reverses an earlier owner decision (pipeline human gate grill: Stop stays visible as a secondary danger action) unless you keep it.
questions.context:
Planned buttons per state (everything else, including Diff, Archive, Unarchive, Stop-extra and Delete…, moves into `⋯`, which opens the existing right-click menu):

| State | Visible |
| --- | --- |
| backlog / ready | `Run` · ⋯ |
| running | `Stop` (destructive, as today) · ⋯ |
| awaiting | `Answer (N) →` · ⋯ |
| review | `Open` · `✓ Done` · ⋯ |
| done / archived | `Open` · ⋯ |
| gate pending | `Review` · `Open` · ⋯ ← **Stop moves into ⋯** |

evidence.label: today's gate-pending row and the earlier decision

options.label: Table as shown: Stop goes into ⋯ on a pending gate
options.consequence: Consistent: running is the only state with a visible Stop. Supersedes the earlier gate decision; `pipelines-human-step.spec` retargets its Stop click.

options.label: Table, but a pending gate keeps a visible Stop (compact danger icon)
options.consequence: Keeps the earlier gate decision; that row is Review · Open · ■ · ⋯ (fits in 233 px).

recommendation.reason: You chose 'primary only'; a gate is a decision point, and stopping the whole pipeline from it is rare and destructive, so one extra click is a fair guard.

questions.title: Keyboard: Enter/Space open the card AND start a keyboard drag. Which key does what?
questions.why: You picked both 'Enter/Space opens' and keyboard dragging; dnd-kit's KeyboardSensor starts a drag on Space and Enter by default, so they collide.
questions.context: The board has no ordering within a column (drops only change the column), so a keyboard drag moves left/right between columns. Screen-reader announcements are dnd-kit's built-in live region, with our own wording.

options.label: Enter opens; Space picks up / drops; ← → move between columns; Esc cancels
options.consequence: The common board convention (Trello, GitHub Projects); Space no longer opens.

options.label: Enter and Space open; a modifier shortcut (e.g. ⌥← / ⌥→) moves the card one column
options.consequence: No pick-up mode; it's a move command, not a drag.

options.label: Enter/Space start a drag (dnd-kit default); `O` opens
options.consequence: Opening a card by keyboard needs a non-standard key.

recommendation.reason: Enter = activate, Space = grab is the convention screen-reader users expect on boards, and it keeps both of your picks.
